t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in editorial magazine style. The frame is split: a narrow warm limestone panel on the left, deep navy on the rest. A giant light-weight sans headline is cropped off the top-left edge and straddles the split, its letters inverting colour as they cross. Across both panels, a three-column fact table with hairline rules and slash-numbered uppercase row labels for <CONTENT>. On the right, one small pale blue-white hairline line drawing of an equipment skid with circled numbered callouts. Square corners, flat, generous space.
signature_idea: A giant cropped headline straddles a limestone-navy split, the letters inverting colour as they cross it, with the fact table bridging both fields.
strengths: colour-inverting cropped headline is a striking, buildable editorial device
fact plus evidence columns suit a facts section for auditors
navy, limestone, light type and hairline rules are on-brand
the line drawing adds equipment context without clutter
weaknesses: table crossing the split hurts legibility at the boundary
line drawing is small and its callouts point to nothing labelled
invented figures, addresses, dates and registration numbers would be mistaken for facts
no steel-blue accent; large dead navy area bottom right
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone with a light oversized headline, hairline rules and square corners fit well, though the table over the split and the invented facts weaken it.
